notes: Reported 2026-05-13: IonQ's first 256-qubit 6th-generation chip-based trapped-ion system 'has left the lab' and is in transit to University of Cambridge Cavendish Laboratory (Ray Dolby Centre). Partnership announced 2026-03-11 (captured in prior scans). 6th-gen design uses electronics rather than lasers for qubit control, leveraging semiconductor manufacturing. No gate fidelity benchmark released for the 256q system yet — Tempo (#AQ 64, 99.99% 2Q fidelity) is the current performance record but uses fewer qubits. If 256q maintains Tempo-level fidelity, it enables 8+ layer MERA circuits. NOTES: Physical delivery vs operational deployment date TBD. No fidelity claims made for the 256q system as shipped. Availability: research access (Cambridge partnership only at this stage). RELEVANCE TO OUR WORK: If 256q system achieves Tempo-level 99.99% 2Q fidelity after commissioning, it becomes the strongest NISQ platform for deep MERA holographic circuits (L=768 sites, 8+ layers). Monitor commissioning results.
